title: Punjab Burns as ED Arrests Minister Sanjeev Arora
excerpt: AAP and BJP workers clash across Punjab cities after Enforcement Directorate takes industries minister into custody on money-laundering charges.
body:
Punjab's streets turned into battlegrounds on Sunday, May 11, after AAP and BJP workers staged rival protests in cities across the state following the Enforcement Directorate's arrest of Cabinet Minister Sanjeev Arora on Saturday in a money-laundering case.

**What happened — the arrest and its trigger:**
The ED arrested Punjab's industries minister Sanjeev Arora in connection with an ongoing Rs 100 crore money-laundering probe linked to alleged fraudulent GST transactions, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). According to the agency, fake GST purchase invoices worth over Rs 100 crore were generated through shell firms in Delhi to fraudulently claim Input Tax Credit, with funds allegedly routed through Dubai and brought back to India in a round-tripping arrangement. Arora is the first minister in Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's Cabinet to be arrested by the ED.

**The clashes — rival protests erupt statewide:**
Tension prevailed in several parts of Punjab on Sunday after workers of the ruling AAP and the BJP came face to face during protests over Arora's arrest. The sharpest confrontation unfolded in Ludhiana, where AAP workers gathered outside the BJP office, BJP activists allegedly threw brooms at AAP protesters, and both sides burnt effigies of each other's leaders. AAP accused the BJP-led Centre of misusing law enforcement agencies against opposition leaders, while BJP leaders demanded the resignation of Arora and Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.

**The political stakes — a pre-election powder keg:**
Arora's arrest comes less than a year before Punjab is scheduled to go to the polls in February 2027. AAP leaders including national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab prabhari Manish Sisodia hailed Arora for allegedly refusing to join the BJP despite pressure. The Gurugram sessions court granted the ED a seven-day remand of Arora after the agency produced him before the court on Saturday.

**What to watch next:**
With Arora's remand running through mid-May and Punjab assembly elections less than nine months away, how Mann's government manages this crisis — and whether more ED actions follow — will define AAP's political footing in its only state stronghold.
